before.title: 1.2 Kappa Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Rattle
before.description: The chain-driven 1.2 Kappa petrol engine in the i20 is prone to timing chain stretch and tensioner wear, particularly on cars with extended oil-change intervals or low oil pressure. Owners report a rattle or whining from the timing cover, worst on cold start, and in documented cases the chain stretched beyond the tensioner's full travel and began jumping teeth on the sprockets. If left unaddressed the chain can skip timing, bending valves and causing major engine damage.
before.solution: Replace the complete timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides, and sprockets if worn) and address any underlying oil-pressure or servicing issue. Using quality oil and the correct OEM-spec oil filter, with shorter change intervals, helps the hydraulic tensioner maintain pressure and prevents recurrence.
symptoms: Metallic rattle from the engine on cold start
Whining or chain noise that rises with engine speed
Noise persisting after tensioner replacement
Rough running or misfire if the chain skips
Check engine light with cam/crank correlation faults

before.title: 7-Speed Dual-Clutch (7DCT) Judder, Hesitation and Overheating
before.description: i20s with the 1.0 T-GDi engine and dry-clutch 7-speed DCT (GB facelift and BC3 generations) commonly exhibit judder and hesitation from a standstill and transmission overheating warnings in heavy stop-and-go traffic. Because the dry clutches have no oil bath for cooling, repeated creeping causes the clutch packs to overheat, triggering shudder, limp behavior and accelerated clutch wear; early Indian-market cars saw overheating failures before Hyundai revised the calibration. Hyundai issued TCU software updates with judder-detection logic for this transmission family.
before.solution: Have the dealer apply the latest TCU software update, which adds judder detection and improved clutch control; juddering clutch packs that are worn or glazed are replaced under warranty. Owners can reduce recurrence by avoiding prolonged clutch-creep in queues and letting the gearbox cool when an overheat warning appears.
symptoms: Shudder or vibration when accelerating from a stop
Hesitation or delayed engagement at junctions
Transmission overheating warning in slow traffic
Jerky low-speed creep in stop-and-go driving
Reduced power or limp mode until the gearbox cools

before.title: Air Conditioning Compressor and Evaporator Failures (Hot-Climate / India Market)
before.description: i20s operated in hot climates, especially Indian-market cars, show a recurring pattern of AC faults: failed compressor control valves causing intermittent or weak cooling, evaporator cores icing over and blocking airflow, and faulty evaporator temperature thermistors. Team-BHP documented cases where the evaporator coil, thermistor and compressor control valve all had to be replaced together on an Elite i20, and complete compressor seizures shortly after the warranty period are commonly reported. The result is AC that cools at first then blows warm, or stops working entirely in peak summer.
before.solution: Diagnose before replacing the whole compressor: a failed compressor control valve or evaporator thermistor is a far cheaper fix and resolves many intermittent-cooling cases. Icing evaporators need the thermistor replaced and the system evacuated, leak-checked and recharged; full compressor or evaporator replacement is the fix for seized or leaking units.
symptoms: AC cools initially then blows warm air after 20-30 minutes
Weak cooling in high ambient temperatures
Airflow from vents drops as evaporator ices over
AC works one day and not the next
Compressor stops engaging entirely

before.title: Clutch Judder and Premature Clutch Wear (Gearbox Input Shaft Oil Seal Leak)
before.description: Manual i20s suffer widely reported clutch judder and premature clutch failure, with documented cases at 5,000-15,500 miles and some owners on their third clutch within two years. A leaking gearbox input shaft (first motion shaft) oil seal contaminates the clutch friction plate with oil, causing judder on take-off and slip; the underlying seal defect was acknowledged in several warranty repairs. Dealers frequently blamed driving style and charged diagnosis fees until independent garages identified the oil contamination.
before.solution: Replace the leaking input shaft oil seal together with a new clutch kit, since a contaminated friction plate cannot be salvaged. If the car is within warranty, insist the seal leak is inspected before accepting a wear-and-tear verdict; aftermarket Exedy kits have a better reputation among owners than some pattern parts.
symptoms: Juddering or shuddering when pulling away from a stop
Clutch slip under load, especially in higher gears
Burning smell after hill starts or towing
Clutch failure at unusually low mileage
Oil residue inside the bellhousing on inspection

before.title: Fuel Pump Impeller Failure — Engine Stall Recall (51DT07, RAPEX Alert 40/2025)
before.description: Hyundai recalled 181,726 i20, i20 N and Bayon vehicles built between 1 April 2021 and early January 2023 (recall code 51DT07, EU Safety Gate/RAPEX alert 40/2025) because the fuel pump impeller can swell at high operating temperatures and from fuel exposure. The swollen impeller contacts the pump housing, causing reduced fuel delivery, sudden loss of engine power, stalling, or a no-start. An unexpected stall in traffic increases the risk of a collision, which is why the campaign was issued as a safety recall across Europe.
before.solution: The fuel pump is replaced free of charge under Hyundai recall campaign 51DT07. Owners of 2021-2023 i20/i20 N/Bayon vehicles should check their VIN with a Hyundai dealer or the national recall register and have the work done promptly.
symptoms: Sudden loss of engine power while driving
Engine stalling without warning
Engine cranks but will not start
Hesitation or sputtering under acceleration
Check engine light with low fuel pressure faults

proposal.title: Fuel Pump Impeller Failure — Engine Stall Recall (51DT07, RAPEX Alert 40/2025)
proposal.description: EU Safety Gate alert SR/03401/25 covers Hyundai i20, i20 N and Bayon vehicles under campaign 51DT07. The alert says the fuel-pump impeller can swell from fuel exposure and high operating temperatures until it contacts the pump housing. Fuel delivery can then fall, causing loss of engine power or the vehicle to stop and increasing injury risk.
proposal.solution: Ask an authorized Hyundai dealer to check the VIN for campaign 51DT07. Hyundai's Slovenia recall notice says the free remedy replaces the fuel pump and tube assembly. It lists regular i20 and Bayon production from April 1, 2021 through December 3, 2022, and i20 N production from June 1, 2021 through January 4, 2023.
symptoms: Loss of engine power
Vehicle may stop because fuel-pump performance is reduced
